problem_statement: When ostest is built with CONFIG_SCHED_EVENTS=y and CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT=y, the test change compiles nxevent.c and invokes nxevent_test from ostest_main. That test includes <nuttx/event.h> and expects the kernel event-group API, including nxevent_t, NXEVENT_INITIALIZER, nxevent_init, nxevent_destroy, nxevent_reset, nxevent_post, nxevent_wait, nxevent_tickwait, and nxevent_trywait, along with flags such as NXEVENT_WAIT_ALL. With the base kernel, the build fails with a missing-header error for nuttx/event.h, so nxevent_test cannot be built or run. The observed problem is therefore a missing public event-group interface in the kernel when the event configuration is enabled. The expected behavior is that the kernel supports the event-group semantics exercised by the test: initialization and reset of event masks, posting that merges or sets events, waiting for any or all specified events, trywait/tickwait returning the matching events or zero when not satisfied, and posting waking waiting tasks, including lower-priority tasks, as exercised by nxevent_test.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: The ostest suite must build and pass a new nxevent test that uses the kernel event-group API (nxevent_init/post/wait/tickwait/trywait/reset/destroy, the NXEVENT_INITIALIZER initializer, and the NXEVENT_WAIT_ALL flag) guarded by CONFIG_SCHED_EVENTS && CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT. On the old kernel these symbols and the CONFIG_SCHED_EVENTS option do not exist, so the test does not build; the task is to provide the kernel nxevent event-group facility so the test compiles and its assertions pass.
